AK.name: Alaska
AK.note: Sullivan seeks a 3rd term; Peltola, a former U.S. Rep, has out-run the top of the ticket here before.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.note: Open — Tuberville is running for governor instead. Not competitive.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.note: Cotton seeks a 3rd term in a reliably Republican state.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.note: Hickenlooper seeks a 2nd term in a Democratic-leaning state.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.note: Coons seeks re-election without a serious Republican challenger.

FL.name: Florida
FL.note: Special election for Rubio's remaining term. Sabato moved it to Safe R on Aug. 19 after Democrats nominated a more progressive candidate.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.note: Ossoff has an enormous financial edge (10-to-1 cash on hand) after winning his 2021 runoff by just over a point.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.note: Open — Ernst is retiring. Cook moved this to Toss-up on Aug. 20; Sabato and Inside Elections still call it Safe/Solid R — one of the widest analyst splits of the cycle.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.note: Risch seeks re-election in a reliably Republican state.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.note: Open — Durbin is retiring after five terms. Reliably Democratic.

KS.name: Kansas
KS.note: Moved from Safe to Likely R on Aug. 4 — a real, if uphill, Democratic opening.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.note: Open — McConnell isn't on a Senate ballot for the first time since 1984. Still Safe R.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.note: Open — Cassidy lost his primary. Reliably Republican.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.note: Markey seeks re-election in a reliably Democratic state.

ME.name: Maine
ME.note: Original Dem nominee Graham Platner exited July 8; a convention chose Troy Jackson 566–5 on July 25 to face Collins.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.note: Open — Peters is retiring. Rogers lost this seat by just 0.34 pts in 2024 running against Slotkin; this is effectively a rematch-caliber toss-up.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.note: Open — Smith is retiring. Flanagan won her primary 59–39 on Aug. 11; MN hasn't elected a GOP senator since 2002.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.note: Hyde-Smith seeks re-election in a reliably Republican state.

MT.name: Montana
MT.note: Open — Daines is running for governor instead. Sabato moved it Likely→Safe R on Aug. 12.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.note: Open — Tillis is retiring. Sabato flipped this to Lean D on Aug. 19; Cook and Inside Elections still call it Lean R — the biggest analyst disagreement of the cycle, and the polling gap is even wider (see Polling tab).

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.note: Independent Dan Osborn lost by 6.7 pts to Fischer in 2024 and is running again — no Democrat on the ballot. Osborn hasn't committed to caucusing with either party if elected, which the model below treats as a genuine wildcard, not a Democratic seat.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.note: Open — Shaheen is retiring. Primary is Sept. 8; Sununu's entry improved GOP odds but didn't flip the rating.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.note: Booker seeks re-election in a reliably Democratic state.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.note: Luján seeks re-election in a reliably Democratic state.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.note: Special election for Vance's remaining term. Sabato moved this to Toss-up on Aug. 19 as Brown's comeback bid gained steam.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.note: Special election after a mid-term Senate vacancy. Reliably Republican.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.note: Merkley seeks re-election in a reliably Democratic state.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.note: Reed seeks re-election in a reliably Democratic state.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.note: Seat opened when Sen. Lindsey Graham died in office on Jul. 11. Deep-red state; not seen as competitive.

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.note: Rounds seeks re-election in a reliably Republican state.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.note: Hagerty seeks re-election in a reliably Republican state.

TX.name: Texas
TX.note: Open — Paxton unseated 4-term Sen. Cornyn in the primary. Cook moved this to Toss-up on Aug. 20 after a run of close polls; Sabato and Inside Elections still treat Texas' Republican lean as decisive and rate it Safe/Solid R — the widest rating-vs-polling gap on this map.

VA.name: Virginia
VA.note: Warner seeks re-election in a Democratic-leaning state.

WV.name: West Virginia
WV.note: Capito seeks re-election in a reliably Republican state.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.note: Open — Lummis is retiring. Reliably Republican.
